summary: Derivation (PROVED, elementary): with the FUNCTIONFIELD_ES §2 Type II chart (a,b,c,d), m = Acd, the identity (ma−1)(mb−1) = A c² d P + 1 gives N_II(P) = Σ_{c,d monic} #{f | Ac²dP+1 monic : f ≡ −1 (mod Acd), gcd(a,b) = 1} — a restricted divisor sum (twin of FRONTIER §2.1 divisor form), not a class-number sum; class numbers can enter only through the character average (main term). Numerical test, q = 3, A ∈ {T, T², T²+1}, ALL irreducible P of degree 9 and 11 (2184 / 16104 P; N_II reproduces ffl_es.c exactly at n = 5, 7; h(P) = L(1,χ_P) from the L-polynomial, brute-force checked at n = 5, 7): N_II is not a function of (P mod A, h(P)) (1998 of 2285 such groups at A = T², n = 11 contain several N_II values); the FF twin of BM_LVALUE Thm A holds strongly (corr(T(P), (h/q^g)²) = −0.98…−0.99, T = Σ(−ab/P)/Φ(Aab)); within P mod A, corr(N_II, h/q^g) = +0.24…+0.54 (EVIDENCE). But after also conditioning on the Legendre symbols of P at the 6 monic irreducibles of degree ≤ 2 the correlation falls to +0.05…+0.11 — the class-number dependence is the small-prime residue effect (cf. RESIDUE_HARDNESS), not an independent class-number law.
not_done: No exact identity with h(D) for P-dependent discriminants D (e.g. disc. of forms representing Ac²dP+1) was searched beyond the (P mod A, h(P)) test; even n (real quadratic, regulator) and q ≥ 5 not run; the divisor-form identity was derived, not separately machine-checked; genus/complex character split of N_II not computed.
next: None for ES; if revisited, compute the real-character (genus) part of N_II and check that it alone carries the h-correlation.

summary: Premise: the Galois-orbit equation Tr_{K/Q}(1/x) = 4/p (x ∈ O_K totally positive, K cyclic cubic) is a variant, not a reformulation of ES over Z (x ∈ Z would give 3/x = 4/p); writing Tr(1/x) = s2(x)/N(x) it is p·s2(x) = 4N(x), and for p INERT in K this forces x = p·y with Tr(1/y) = 4, i.e. it is p-independent: solvable for all inert p iff some totally positive z ∈ O_K has Tr(1/z) ∈ 4ℤ_{>0} (PROVED, elementary; x = p(Tr(1/z)/4)z). Search (conductors 7, 9, 13, 19, box |coords| ≤ 60, ~4·10⁵ totally positive x each; also 31, 43, 73 box 40): every prime p ≤ 10⁴ solved is split in K (cond. 7: all split p ≤ 139 hit, no inert or ramified p ever), and NO totally positive z has 4 | Tr(1/z) (integral Tr(1/z) occurs 51–187 times per field with residues 1, 2, 3 mod 4), while without positivity 4 | Tr(1/z) is common (258 cases, cond. 7, box 25) and in non-cyclic totally real cubics m = Tr(1/z) ≡ 0 (4) is abundant (34 768 polys for m = 4, a ≤ 120) but cyclic (square disc) has 0 for m = 4, 8, 12, 16 vs 2–31 for every other m ≤ 16 (EVIDENCE). CONJECTURE: a positivity-dependent, cyclic-specific obstruction 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) (in fact Tr(z)·Tr(1/z) ≢ 0 (mod 4) in all 75 cyclic hits) blocks every inert prime; PROVED for units when 2 is inert and totally positive units are squares (F₈ trace argument: Tr(w̄) = Tr(w̄⁻¹) = 0 impossible).
not_done: No proof of the mod-4 obstruction for non-units (2-adic discriminant analysis shows it is not a 2-adic condition on D alone: D ≡ 1 mod 8 is possible; Hilbert-symbol/trace-form route not completed); split primes beyond the box (p > ~300) not solved, so 'all split p solvable' is untested beyond ~139; only Z[θ] (index 2/3 orders) for conductors 31, 43, 73.
next: Try to prove 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) for totally positive z in cyclic cubic fields via am − 9 = Tr((z−σz)²/(zσz)) (u totally positive, N(u) = (Δ/c)²) or a Hasse-invariant computation of Tr(y v²); it would be a clean positivity+reciprocity obstruction of the type ES lacks (Bright–Loughran).

summary: Did the lift: the complete F₂[T] covering for A = T² (data/review_ffl/cover_q2_A100.txt, 4 leaves, E ∈ {1, T+1}, a = 1, b = P; Thm 6.1 is its T+1 branch) under T ↦ 2 with all sign lifts (e ∈ {±1, ±3}, a = ±1, b = ±n). Every lift is the universal identity 4/n = 1/X + 1/Y + 1/Z, X = (n+e)/4, κ = (a+b)/e, i.e. an Elsholtz–Tao Type II e-slice; positive lifts exist only on n ≡ 3 (mod 4) (e = 1) and n ≡ 5 (mod 12) (e = 3), while n ≡ 1 (mod 12) — which contains all six Mordell-hard classes mod 840 — gets only the signed identity 4/n = 1/X + 1/(κX) − 1/(κnX), X = (n+3)/4, κ = (n−1)/3, whose negative term is ≤ 3/n² of 4/n (PROVED, exact rational check). The 'positivity repair' 1/(κX) − 1/(κnX) = 3/(nX) = 1/y + 1/z is possible iff X = (n+3)/4 has a prime factor ≡ 2 (mod 3), i.e. exactly the ET e = 3 slice: it works for 130 261 / 166 011 = 78.5 % of primes p ≡ 1 (12) ≤ 10⁷ but only 8 590 / 20 513 = 41.9 % of Mordell-hard primes (first failures 73, 193, 241, 313, 409; EVIDENCE) — the char-2 shadow re-derives a known slice, no new mechanism.
not_done: Lifts of the A = T⁴, T⁴+1 coverings (they specialise to 16/n at T = 2, not ES) and of degree-3 A not done; T ↦ t ≠ 2 only checked by hand for A = T (t = 4) and A = T+1 (t = 3), which give the trivial class n ≡ 3 (mod 4); repair via other splittings of the negative term (not through 3/(nX)) not searched.
next: None (the lift lands on the ET e = 3 slice).
